title: Octavian, Caesar's Heir
objective: After this level you can explain how Caesar's young heir built power after the assassination.
summary: Caesar’s will made his 18-year-old great-nephew Octavian his heir. Octavian joined Antony and Lepidus, and they crushed the assassins at Philippi.

cards.headline: Caesar’s will named an heir almost no one expected: an 18-year-old.
The heir
cards.body: Caesar’s will adopted his 18-year-old great-nephew Octavian as his son and heir. Octavian took the name Gaius Julius Caesar and used it to win over Caesar’s soldiers and supporters. The name was his greatest asset.

cards.headline: Three men again
cards.body: In 43 BCE Octavian, Mark Antony and Lepidus formed the Second Triumvirate, an alliance given legal power for five years. At Philippi in 42 BCE, Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius, who both took their own lives.
cards.callout: Unlike the First, the Second Triumvirate was legal

cards.fact: Cicero was killed in the proscriptions of 43 BCE.
cards.context: The triumvirs revived Sulla’s lists of enemies. Cicero had attacked Antony in fierce speeches, and his name was on the list.

cards.headline: The heir: rising
learned: Caesar adopted Octavian in his will
The Second Triumvirate formed in 43 BCE

questions.prompt: How was Octavian related to Julius Caesar?

options.label: Caesar’s great-nephew, adopted in his will
His younger brother, a fellow general
options.rationale: He was a generation or two younger.

options.label: His son by Cleopatra, born in Egypt
His rival general in Gaul
options.rationale: Octavian was a teenager when Caesar died.

questions.explanation: Caesar’s will adopted his great-nephew Octavian as his son and heir.

questions.prompt: Why did Caesar’s name matter so much to Octavian?

options.label: It made him consul automatically at 18
It won over Caesar’s soldiers and supporters
It let him skip the Senate’s approval
It made the assassins surrender
options.rationale: He had to defeat them in battle.

questions.explanation: Caesar’s veterans and supporters rallied to the man who carried his name.

questions.prompt: From Level 40: whom did Antony and Octavian defeat at Philippi in 42 BCE?

options.label: Catiline and his fellow plotters
options.rationale: Cicero dealt with them in 63 BCE.

questions.explanation: Brutus and Cassius, who led the plot against Caesar, were defeated at Philippi.
